United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Enhancing protection of cultural heritage in Ukraine: from emergency response to recovery

description.narrative: The project to support the safeguarding of Ukraine’s cultural heritage in the context of the ongoing war by addressing urgent protection needs and ensuring that culture and heritage are systematically integrated into recovery planning processes. It will support the systematic monitoring and verification of war-related damage to cultural heritage, including World Heritage properties, through remote and satellite imagery analysis complemented by field verification, and will enable timely emergency stabilization and repair interventions at war-damaged cultural properties to prevent further deterioration. In parallel, the project will support the development and promotion of policy guidance, planning tools, and regulatory frameworks to ensure that cultural heritage and the culture sector are effectively reflected in national and local recovery and reconstruction frameworks. The project is aligned with UNESCO’s mandate and normative instruments in the field of culture - including the 1954 and 1972 Conventions - and contributes to the implementation of the 2015 Strategy for the Reinforcement of UNESCO’s Action for the Protection of Culture and the Promotion of Cultural Pluralism in the Event of Armed Conflict, the 2025 Recommendation concerning the protection and promotion of museums and collections, their diversity and their role in society, and the MONDIACULT 2022 Declaration and the subsequent Outcome Document MONDIACULT 2025. It also supports the priorities under the Action Plan for Culture in Ukraine, developed by the Ministry of Culture and UNESCO and endorsed by international and national partners in 2024; Ukraine’s Strategy for the Development of Culture 2025-2030 (adopted in March 2025); and the Government of Japan’s commitment to Ukraine’s recovery.
